title: External global derived Hom evaluation respects coefficient cones
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X,Y,P$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $a:P\to X$, $b:P\to Y$ be scheme morphisms. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites in a common module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse image is the constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and all tensor products are derived with the direct-sum total convention [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and suppose $F=a^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}L$ is bounded below. Let $E$ on $X$ and $H$ on $Y$ be bounded cochain complexes of flat $A$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For any complex $G$ on a scheme $T$ and bounded-below $M$, write
$$\mathsf H_T(G,M)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_A(G,M))\in D(A),$$
where $R\mathcal Hom$ is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $R\Gamma$ means right-derived global sections. Equivalently this is represented by the complex of global morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_T(G,I)$ for a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$, with the Hom differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. Write $\underline Q_T$ for the termwise constant sheaf complex associated to an $A$-complex $Q$.

There is a canonical morphism
$$\lambda_{E,H}:\mathsf H_X(E,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)\longrightarrow\mathsf H_P(a^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H,F).$$
It is the transpose, for global derived Hom and constant sheaves, of the two evaluation maps $\underline{\mathsf H_X(E,K)}_X\otimes_A^LE\to K$ and $\underline{\mathsf H_Y(H,L)}_Y\otimes_A^LH\to L$, pulled back to $P$ and tensored with the Koszul interchange. The Koszul normalization is specified on resolving evaluation maps, as follows. Choose K-injective representatives $I_K,I_L$ and K-flat resolutions with flat terms
$$U\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I_K),\qquad V\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_Y(H,I_L).$$
The resulting chain evaluations are $t_X:\underline U_X\otimes_A E\to I_K$ and $t_Y:\underline V_Y\otimes_A H\to I_L$. Choose factorizations [lem-pur-kflat-map-factorization]
$$\underline U_X\otimes_A E\xrightarrow{u}N_K\xrightarrow{c_K}I_K,\qquad
\underline V_Y\otimes_A H\xrightarrow{v}N_L\xrightarrow{c_L}I_L,$$
with $N_K,N_L$ K-flat with flat terms, $c_K,c_L$ quasi-isomorphisms, and $c_Ku\simeq t_X$, $c_Lv\simeq t_Y$ by chain homotopies. Put $T=a^{-1}N_K\otimes_A b^{-1}N_L$, which represents $F$, and choose a K-injective resolution $i:T\to J$. Then $\lambda_{E,H}$ is represented by the chain map
$$U\otimes_A V\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_P(a^{-1}E\otimes_A b^{-1}H,J),$$
whose local evaluation on homogeneous $w\in U^r$, $z\in V^s$, $e\in(a^{-1}E)^q$, $h\in b^{-1}H$ is
$$ (w\otimes z)(e\otimes h)=(-1)^{sq}i\bigl(a^{-1}u(w\otimes e)\otimes b^{-1}v(z\otimes h)\bigr).$$
Here constant sections supply the $w,z$ on $P$; all pullback comparisons are the canonical ones. This represents the derived transpose for every such choice. In particular the formula uses K-flat targets for the two lifted evaluations, rather than the ordinary tensor of the two K-injective representatives.

The morphisms $\lambda_{E,H}$ are natural contravariantly in $E,H$ and covariantly in $K,L$, and commute with open restriction of $X$ or $Y$ and the induced restriction of $P$. For fixed $H$, if $E_2\to E_1\to E_0\to E_2[1]$ is a distinguished triangle represented by bounded flat complexes, the three maps $\lambda_{E_0,H},\lambda_{E_1,H},\lambda_{E_2,H}$ form a morphism of distinguished triangles from
$$\mathsf H_X(E_0,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)\longrightarrow\mathsf H_X(E_1,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)\longrightarrow\mathsf H_X(E_2,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$$
to the contravariant global-Hom triangle of $a^{-1}E_i\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H$ into $F$. The same assertion holds with $E$ fixed and a triangle in $H$. Distinguished triangles and shifts use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-triangulated-category]. In particular these are the specified evaluation maps on all three terms, including the cone term, and the square on the connecting morphism commutes. In the first case the right-tensor shift comparison is $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$; in the second case the left-tensor shift comparison is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(x)}x\otimes y$.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated; section-internal-hom and section-hom-complexes. The external global-Hom evaluation transformation and its compatibility with both coefficient cones are an agent-formulated refinement of the Hom-complex constructions.

proof.text: The bounded flat complexes $E,H$ are K-flat by the bounded-above-flat lemma for sites. Choose K-injective representatives $I_K,I_L$ using existence of K-injective resolutions. The sections-model theorem gives $C_E=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I_K)$ and $D_H=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_Y(H,I_L)$ as representatives of the two global derived Hom objects. Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $U\to C_E$, $V\to D_H$, using the one-object ringed site for $A$-complexes. Constant sheaves are left adjoint to sections by the existing module-valued constant-sheaf node. The constant functor is exact by the constant-projection construction; as pullback from the point ringed topos it preserves flat-term K-flat complexes by the ringed-topos pullback theorem. Scheme inverse images have the same preservation property and are exact on constant-$A$ modules. Thus ordinary pullback computes the required derived pullbacks.

Write $C=\mathsf H_X(E,K)$ and $D=\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$. Compose the derived global-sections counit with internal evaluation to obtain $\mathrm{ev}_X:\underline C_X\otimes^L E\to K$ and $\mathrm{ev}_Y:\underline D_Y\otimes^L H\to L$. The derived constant/sections adjunction is the one specified by the constant-projection node. Its composite with the closed tensor--Hom adjunction gives the bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q,\mathsf H_P(G,F))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P,A)}(\underline Q_P\otimes^L G,F).$$
Use it to define $\lambda$ as the unique transpose of
$$\underline{C\otimes^LD}_P\otimes^L(a^{-1}E\otimes^Lb^{-1}H)\xrightarrow{\chi}
(a^{-1}\underline C_X\otimes^La^{-1}E)\otimes^L(b^{-1}\underline D_Y\otimes^Lb^{-1}H)
\xrightarrow{a^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_X\otimes^Lb^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_Y}F.$$
Here $\chi$ uses constant-complex pullback comparisons and moves $\underline D$ past $a^{-1}E$ with the Koszul symmetry. Constants commute with inverse image degreewise, and strong-monoidal pullback supplies the tensor comparisons. These are derived arrows throughout.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and section-internal-hom: adjunction and evaluation; agent expansion of blueprint support comparison.

proof.text: The chain map $t_X:\underline U_X\otimes E\to I_K$ sends $w\otimes e$ to the evaluation of the image of $w$ in $C_E$. Its differential identity follows from $d(f)=d_If-(-1)^{|f|}fd_E$: the two terms containing $fd_E$ cancel in $t_Xd$. Thus the unsigned evaluation is a chain map. The tensor--Hom isomorphism and the constant-sheaf adjunction identify its localization with $\mathrm{ev}_X$; likewise for $t_Y$. Its source is K-flat: for any acyclic $Z$, first $E\otimes Z$ and then $\underline U\otimes(E\otimes Z)$ are acyclic. Its terms are flat: tensor of two flat modules has exact tensor functor by composition, and in each total degree only finitely many terms occur because $E$ is bounded; finite sums preserve flatness. Likewise for $H$. Apply the new factorization lemma to $t_X,t_Y$, including its flat-terms clause, obtaining exactly $u,c_K,v,c_L$ in the statement. Their homotopy identities give $Q(c_K)Q(u)=Q(t_X)$ and $Q(c_L)Q(v)=Q(t_Y)$ after localization.

The pullbacks of $N_K,N_L$ are K-flat with flat terms. Their ordinary tensor $T$ therefore computes $F$ by the tensor-descent theorem. Choose $i:T\to J$ K-injective. The composite
$$\underline{U\otimes V}_P\otimes(a^{-1}E\otimes b^{-1}H)\xrightarrow{\chi}
a^{-1}(\underline U_X\otimes E)\otimes b^{-1}(\underline V_Y\otimes H)
\xrightarrow{a^{-1}u\otimes b^{-1}v}T\xrightarrow{i}J$$
is a chain map; the interchange contributes exactly $(-1)^{|z||e|}$. Uncurrying/currying gives the displayed chain map from $U\otimes V$ to the global Hom complex. The latter represents the target by the sections-model theorem. The source represents $C\otimes_A^LD$ since $U,V$ are K-flat. Under the canonical identifications, $Q(c_K)Q(u)=Q(t_X)$ and $Q(c_L)Q(v)=Q(t_Y)$ imply that its derived uncurrying is precisely the composite of Step 2: tensor these equalities with the derived tensor bifunctor and apply the natural pullback constraints. The adjunction bijection is injective, so this is $\lambda$. This proves the normalization and independence of all lifts and resolutions. No inverse comparison from $a^{-1}I_K\otimes b^{-1}I_L$ occurs.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, 0G7D, 0A90, 08J9; section-hom-complexes. Agent construction of a valid model for the transpose.

proof.text: The composite in Step 2 is contravariantly natural in $E,H$ and covariantly natural in $K,L$: these are the four naturalities of evaluation and tensor. The adjunction bijection is natural, so its transposes have the same naturalities. For an open restriction of $X$ (or $Y$), use the induced restriction of $P$. Restriction commutes with internal Hom by the exact-restriction theorem, and it commutes with the constant complex and the monoidal pullbacks. The map on global Hom is induced by restriction of global morphisms in the sections model. On an evaluation $f(e)$ its restriction is $(f|)(e|)$; consequently the two uncurried restriction composites agree. Their transposes agree by injectivity of the same bijection. This proves the specified restriction square, without making a natural choice of $u$ or $v$.

For fixed $H,K,L$, both $A(E)=\mathsf H_X(E,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$ and $B(E)=\mathsf H_P(a^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H,F)$ are exact contravariant functors. Indeed internal Hom is contravariantly exact, right-derived global sections is triangulated, exact module inverse image is triangulated, and derived tensor is exact in each variable with its canonical shift comparisons. These assertions apply in the ambient unbounded categories; the bounded hypotheses in the item are more than enough for the Hom models. The same reasoning gives exact contravariant functors of $H$ when $E$ is fixed. It remains to show that the natural transformation of Step 5 commutes with their shift comparisons; mere naturality does not imply that. Steps 7--9 check this on the valid model of Step 4.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); derived tensor and right-derived-functor exactness.

proof.text:
For any complex $B$ and K-injective $I$, the first-variable Hom shift is the chain isomorphism
$$\theta_B:\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B[1],I)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,I)[-1],\qquad
(\theta_B f)^p=(-1)^n f^{p-1}\quad(|f|=n).$$
Substitution in $df=d_If-(-1)^nfd_B$, with $d_{B[1]}=-d_B$, proves the chain identity: both sides have components $(-1)^{n+1}d_If-fd_B$. For the representative $U\to C_E$, use $U[-1]\to C_{E[1]}$ defined by $\theta_E^{-1}$ after the shifted resolution map. On the source of evaluation, the map $\eta: \underline{U[-1]}\otimes E[1]\to\underline U\otimes E$ sends $w\otimes e$ to $(-1)^r w\otimes e$ for $w\in U[-1]^r$. Its two differential components are $(-1)^r d_Uw\otimes e$ and $-w\otimes d_Ee$, so it is a chain map. The shifted evaluation is exactly $t_X\eta$. Therefore $u'=u\eta$ and the same $c_K,N_K$ factor this evaluation up to homotopy. Use the identical construction with $V,H,v$ for the second variable. These choices let all shift computations land in the same K-flat tensor $T$ and the same $J$.

source.place: Sections 0A8X and 08J7, Tag 08JC: explicit Hom shift and evaluation signs.

proof.text: For the $E$ shift use $w\in U[-1]^r$, $z\in V^s$, $e\in E[1]^q=E^{q+1}$ and $h\in H$. In the Step-4 formula for $E[1]$, interchange contributes $(-1)^{sq}$ and the shifted lift $u'$ contributes $(-1)^r$. The coefficient identification $E[1]\otimes H\cong(E\otimes H)[1]$ has no sign. Applying $\theta_{E\otimes H}$ to the output Hom map adds $(-1)^{r+s}$, leaving total sign $(-1)^{sq+s}$. In the other composite the source identification $U[-1]\otimes V\cong(U\otimes V)[-1]$ has no sign. The unshifted Step-4 pairing, now evaluated on $e$ of degree $q+1$, has sign $(-1)^{s(q+1)}$. These agree. In both cases the unsigned value is the same $i(a^{-1}u(w\otimes e)\otimes b^{-1}v(z\otimes h))$. The equality holds as chain maps on the tensor summands and hence after localization. This is the shift square for $E$, with the right-tensor shift comparison stated in the item.

source.place: Tags 0A90 and 08JC; agent calculation on the K-flat lifted evaluation model.

proof.text: For the $H$ shift use $w\in U^r$, $z\in V[-1]^s$, $e\in E^q$ and $h\in H[1]$. Interchange contributes $(-1)^{sq}$ and $v'=v\eta$ adds $(-1)^s$. Identifying the coefficient $E\otimes H[1]$ with $(E\otimes H)[1]$ contributes $(-1)^q$ when precomposing the Hom map with the inverse tensor-shift map. Applying the target Hom shift adds $(-1)^{r+s}$. Thus this composite has sign $(-1)^{sq+q+r}$. In the other composite the source identification $U\otimes V[-1]\cong(U\otimes V)[-1]$ contributes $(-1)^r$. The unshifted pairing has second Hom-input degree $s-1$, and contributes $(-1)^{(s-1)q}$. Its total sign is again $(-1)^{sq+q+r}$ and its unsigned value is the same element of $J$. The tensor-shift map is a chain map by substituting $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes dy$; its sign is $(-1)^{|x|}$ for either shift $[1]$ or $[-1]$. This proves the second-variable shift square on a model of $F$, including precisely the left-tensor sign in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0A90 and 08JC; agent calculation on the same K-flat target as Step 8.

proof.text: Apply the exact functors $A,B$ of Step 6 to $E_2\to E_1\to E_0\xrightarrow d E_2[1]$. Naturality of $\lambda$ gives the squares for the first two arrows. For clarity write $s_A:A(E[1])\cong A(E)[-1]$, and similarly $s_B$. The shift square proved in Step 8 is $s_B\lambda_{E[1]}=\lambda_E[-1]s_A$. Naturality at $d$ is $B(d)\lambda_{E_2[1]}=\lambda_{E_0}A(d)$. Shift this equality by $[1]$ and substitute the shift square. This gives $\delta_B\lambda_{E_2}=\lambda_{E_0}[1]\delta_A$, because each connecting map is the shifted map on $d$ composed with its inverse shift comparison (with the same conventional contravariant rotation sign on both sides). Thus the connecting square commutes for the specified cone component, not just some completion of two squares. Applying Step 9 and the same argument to a triangle in $H$ proves the other assertion. No change of representatives is required in this deduction; naturality and the already-proved shift identities are equalities in the derived categories.

source.place: Tag 08JC and the canonical contravariant Hom triangle; agent deduction of both connecting squares.
